spans.s:
जम्भ, अस्, m. the jaws (generally used in plur.);
the mouth, a tooth, an eye-tooth, tusk; one who
crushes or devours, as a demon; N. of several demons;
a leader of the demons in the war against the gods
under Indra; N. of a son of Pra-hrāda; of a son of
Hiraṇya-kaśipu; N. of the father-in-law of Hiraṇya-
kaśipu; N. of the father of Sunda; the citron tree,
= जम्भीर, जम्भल, जम्बीर; eating, food;
biting asunder, opening by biting, explanation, inter-
pretation; a quiver; a part, a portion; (आ), f. opening
of the mouth; [cf. अन्तर्-जम्भ, कु-ज्˚, तपुर्-ज्˚,
तिग्म-ज्˚, तृष्ट-ज्˚, &c.; cf. also Gr. γαμφηλαί.]
—जम्भ-कुण्ड, अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.
—जम्-
भ-द्विष्, ट्, m. the enemy of Jambha, an epithet
of Indra.
—जम्भ-भेदिन्, ई, m. the destroyer of
Jambha, a N. of Indra.
—जम्भ-सुत, अस्, आ, अम्,
Ved. pressed with the jaws, chewed.
—जम्भारि
(˚भ-अरि), इस्, m. ‘the enemy of Jambha,’ Indra;
Indra's thunderbolt; fire.
जम्भ जम्भ. See under 1. जभ्, p. 338.

जाम्भ जाम्भ, अस्, m. a patronymic from
Jambha.

जम्भक, अस्, आ, अम्, crushing, devouring; killing,
destroying; biting asunder; explaining, interpreting;
opening, expanding; yawning; (अस्), m., N. of a
demon or of a despised tribe of men; N. of several
evil spirits supposed to reside in various magical
weapons; N. of a verse addressed to them; N. of a
demon conquered by Kṛṣṇa; N. of an attendant of
Śiva; a lime or citron; (आ), f. opening the mouth.
जम्भन् = जम्भ in तृण-जम्भन्, &c.

1. जम्भन, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. crushing, destroying;
one who crushes.
2. जम्भन, अम्, n. sexual intercourse.
जम्भन जम्भन. See under 1. and 2. जभ्.

जम्भ्य, अस्, m., Ved. an incisor (tooth) or per-
haps a grinder.

जम् 1. जम्, cl. 1. P. जमति, जजाम,
जमितुम्, to eat, consume; to go (?);
to blaze (?); [cf. Hib. diamanu, ‘food, sustenance;’
gion, ‘the mouth:’ Old Germ. gouma, kouma, ‘food;’
gaumo, ‘the palate:’ Mod. Germ. Gaumen.]

जम् 2. जम्, Ved. (used in Inst. ज्मा and
Abl. Gen. ज्मस्), the earth; ज्मा, on earth; [cf. गम्
and क्षम्.]

जमत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, Ved. blazing.
—जमद्-
अग्नि, इस्, m., N. of a Ṛṣi often mentioned together
with Viśvā-mitra as an adversary of Vasiṣṭha, and
according to some a descendant of Bhṛgu; in epic
poetry a son of Bhārgava Ṛcīka and father of
Paraśu-rāma.
जमन, अम्, n. eating; food, victuals.
जमज जम-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, = यम-ज, q. v.
जमदग्नि जमद्-अग्नि. See जमत् above.

जम्पती जम्पती (fr. दम्पती ?, but accord-
ing to some जम् is fr. जाया; cf. Hib. gamh; Gr.
γάμος ?), m. du. wife and husband.
जम्बालिनी, f. a river.

जम्बिर जम्बिर, अस्, m. = जम्बीर, the citron
tree.

जम्बीर, अस्, m. the citron tree or common
lime; a plant called by some a sort of basil with
small leaves, a kind of Ocimum, = मरुवक or
प्रस्थ-पुष्प; (अम्), n. a citron; [cf. जम्-
भीर, जम्भ, जम्भल.]

जाम्बीर जाम्बीर, अम्, n. (fr. जम्बीर), a
citron.
जम्बीरक, अस्, m. a kind of Ocimum.

जम्बु जम्बु, उस्, or जम्बू, ऊस्, f. (said to be
fr. rt. 1. जम्), a fruit tree, the rose apple, Eugenia
Jambolana, or another species of Eugenia; (ऊस्, उ),
f. n. its fruit; (उस्, उ), m. n., N. of a Dvīpa [cf.
जम्बु-द्वीप]; N. of a fabulous river, said to flow
from the mountain Meru and to be formed by the
juice of the fruits of an immense Jambu tree on that
mountain; [cf. आढक-जम्बु, काक-ज्˚, गोरक्ष-
ज्˚.]
—जम्बु-द्वीप or जम्बू-द्वीप, अस्, m., N. of
one of the seven continents or rather large islands
surrounding the mountain Meru; it is so named
either from the Jambu trees abounding in it, or from
an enormous Jambu tree on Mount Meru visible like
a standard to the whole continent, and implies
(according to the Purāṇas) the central division of the
world, or the known world, including India; with
Buddhists it is confined to India; with Jainas it is
one of the five divisions of India.
—जम्बु-ध्वज,
अस्, m. another N. for Jambu-dvīpa (‘having the
Jambu tree as its standard’); N. of a Nāga.
—जम्बु-पर्वत, अस्, m. another N. for Jambu-
dvīpa.
—जम्बु-प्रस्थ, अस्, m., N. of a town.
—जम्बु-मत्, आन्, m. a mountain; a monkey;
(ती), f. an Apsaras or heavenly nymph; [cf. जाम्ब-
वत् and जम्बु-वत्.]
—जम्बु-माल, अस्, m., N. of
a man.
—जम्बु-मालिन्, ई, m., N. of a Rakṣas.
—जम्बु-रुद्र, अस्, m., N. of a serpent-king.
—जम्बु-वन-ज, अम्, n. the white flower of the
China rose.
—जम्बु-सर, अस्, m., N. of a town in
Gurjara (Jumbooseer between Cambay and Baroch).
—जम्बू-खण्ड, अस्, अम्, m. n. another N. for
Jambu-dvīpa.
—जम्बूखण्ड-विनिर्माण-पर्वन्,
अ, n. the first six Adhyāyas of the sixth book of
the Mahā-bhārata.
—जम्बूनद-प्रभ, अस्, m.,
N. of a future Buddha.
—जम्बू-नदी, f., N. of one
of the seven arms of the heavenly Gaṅgā.
—जम्बू-
मार्ग, अस्, अम्, m. n., N. of a Tīrtha (the way
[]
leading to the sacred Jambu on Meru).
—जम्बू-
स्वामिन्, ई, m., N. of the last Arhat of the Jainas.
—जम्ब्व्-ओष्ठ = जाम्बवौष्ठ, q. v.

जम्बुक जम्बुक, अस्, m. a jackal; a low
man; N. of one of the attendants of Skanda; an
epithet of Varuṇa; the plant Eugenia (commonly
called गोलाप जाम); or perhaps a kind of Śyoṇāka;
(आ), f. a female jackal; [cf. जम्बूक.]
—जम्बु-
केश्वर-तीर्थ (˚क-ईश्˚), अम्, n., N. of a Tīrtha.

जम्बूक, अस्, m. a jackal; a low man; N. of one
of the attendants of Skanda; an epithet of Varuṇa;
(आ), f. a kind of grape without stones, = काकली-
द्राक्षा; [cf. जम्बुक and गृध्र-जम्बूक.]

जाम्बुक जाम्बुक, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जम्बुक),
coming from or belonging to a jackal; जाम्बुकं
वचस्, a jackal's cry.

जम्बुल जम्बुल, अस्, m. a kind of disease of
the outer ear; the plant Eugenia Jambolana [cf.
जम्बु]; another plant, Pandanus Odoratissimus;
[cf. केतक; cf. also जम्बूल.]

जम्भर जम्भर, अस्, m. the lime or citron
tree; [cf. the following.]

जम्भल, अस्, m. the lime or citron tree [cf.
जम्बीर]; N. of a Jina or deified Jaina saint; N.
of a man; (आ), f. a female Rākṣasī, by meditating
on whom women become pregnant.
—जम्भल-
दत्त, अस्, m., N. of the supposed author of the
Vetāla-pañca-viṃśati.
जम्भिन्, ई, m. the lime or citron tree.

जम्भीर, अस्, m. the lime or citron tree, appa-
rently of more than one species; a plant considered
to be a kind of basil with small leaves; [cf. जम्-
बीर.]

जम्भलिका जम्भलिका, f. a kind of song.
(जम्भालिका appears to be incorrect.)
जम्व जम्व, अस्, m. mud, mire.

जामदग्निय and जामदग्नेय, a patronymic
from Jamad-agni.

जामदग्न्य, अस्, आ, अम्, belonging to Jamad-
agni or to his son Jāmadagnya; a patronymic; (अस्),
m., N. of a Catur-aha ceremony.

जामर्य जामर्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. (Sāy.) from
जा-अमर्य, making creatures immortal; but per-
haps connected with a rt. जम् for चम् and used as
an epithet of milk.

जामल जामल = यामल in कृष्ण-जामल
&c.

जामा जामा, f. (fr. rt. जन्), a daughter-
in-law.

जा-मातृ, ता, m. (‘the maker of [new] offspring,’
or perhaps related to जामि below), a daughter's
husband, a son-in-law; a husband, a lord or master;
a friend; the sunflower, Heliantus Annuus; [cf.
यामातृ; cf. also Lat. gener (?); Gr. γάμβρος.]
—जामातृ-त्व, अम्, n. the relationship of a
daughter's husband.

जामातृक, अस्, आ, अम्, coming from or belonging
to a daughter's husband; (अस्), m. a daughter's
husband.

जामि, इस्, इस्, इ, Ved. related by blood, con-
sanguineous, (rarely applied to a brother but often to
a sister either with or without the word स्वसृ); re-
lated like brother and sister; (in Vedic language the
fingers are sometimes called जामयः or ‘the sisters;’
the सप्त जामयः or ‘seven sisters’ are the seven
Dhītayas or acts of devotion in the Soma wor-
ship); related in general, belonging to, peculiar
to, customary, usual; (इस्), f. a sister, a virtuous and
respectable woman; (more properly) a female rela-
tive of the head of a family, a daughter-in-law; N.
of a deity; N. of an Apsaras; (ई), n. blood-relation-
ship, consanguinity, the relation of brother and sister,
[]
relation in general, descent; (in grammar and in the
sacrificial language) tautology, repetition; water;
[cf. अ-जामि and देव-ज्˚.]
—जामि-कृत्, त्, त्, त्, Ved.
creating relationship.
—जामि-त्व, अम्, n., Ved. con-
sanguinity, relationship.
—जामि-वत्, ind., Ved. like
a sister or brother.
—जामि-शंस, अस्, m., Ved. the
curse pronounced by a brother or relation.
जामेय, अस्, m. a sister's son.

जामित्र जामित्र, अम्, n. (fr. the Gr. διάμετρον,
in astronomy) the seventh lunar mansion.

जाम्बव जाम्बव, अस्, ई, अम्, coming from or
belonging to the Jambū tree; (अस्), m. = जाम्बवत्,
q. v.; (ई), f., N. of a plant, = नाग-दमनी; (अम्),
n. the fruit of the Jambū tree, the rose-apple; gold;
N. of a town.
—जाम्बवौष्ठ (˚व-ओष्˚), अम्, n.
a cauterizing needle or probe; also जाम्बवोष्ठ,
जाम्बोष्ठ, जाम्बौष्ठ, and जम्ब्व्-ओष्ठ.

जाम्बवक, अस् or अम् (?), m. or n. (?), N. of a
place.

जाम्बवत्, आन्, m. (for जाम्बव-वत् ?), N. of the
chief of the bears who, with the monkeys, was an ally
of Rāma and therefore sometimes called a monkey;
he was a son of Pitāmaha and father of Jāmbavatī
who was wife of Kṛṣṇa and mother of Śāmba; (ती),
f., N. of the daughter of Jāmbavat, wife of Kṛṣṇa
and mother of Śāmba; N. of a plant, = जम्बू.

जाम्बुवत्, आन्, m. = जाम्बवत्; (ती), f. = जाम्ब-
वती.

जाम्बील जाम्बील, अस्, m., Ved. the knee-
bone, knee-pan; (said by some to be so called from
its similarity to a citron, by others considered as
a corruption fr. जानु and बिल.)

जाम्बूनद जाम्बूनद, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. जम्बू-
नदी), coming from or belonging to the river
Jambū, epithet of a kind of gold; made of the
gold called Jāmbūnada, golden; (अस्), m., N. of
a son of Janam-ejaya; N. of a mountain; (ई),
f., N. of a river; (अम्), n. gold from the Jambū.
river, any gold, a golden ornament; N. of a lake;
the thorn-apple.
—जाम्बूनद-मय, अस्, ई, अम्,
made of the gold called Jāmbūnada, golden.
